body.p: There once lived an old woman. She had three sons. In the autumn the sons went to the forest. Having gone off to hunt, they went to hunt. The old woman remained alone. One day she was whiling the day away. âItâs the second morning Iâm sitting around in the morning. It seems that there is something by the door, something by the door. At one time my tent seemed like it started falling over.[BrM:] okon=ukoËn 'earlier'? My tent is leaning to the side. I looked up to see what it is sticking into the tent. Itâs making my tent lean to one side, it looks like. Once a devil showed up in the house. A devil, or what was this? He is beating something against the ground. He took a step forward on the other side and sat down on my sonâs bed. He sat forward a little again. He hurt his knee, his knee, he made ten arrows out of it. He made four (flintstones/matches?). He tore off a piece[BrM:] Cf. Å¡eËqÉ¨ 'thread'.[BrM:] 'É¨ntaËlÊ¼-tÉ¨' ' of the nose and made a vessel for the glue (fish glue). Then in the evening my older son returned home. âChild, you know what? As I was sitting in the morning, after you left, in the street there something by the door. At one time my tent started falling over to the side. My tent started leaning over to the side. I had just looked up, it was a tree or whatever, it was pushing my tent to the side. Ah, once something from the street showed up in the tent. A person or whatever it was, smiling, or maybe laughing. Walking forward along that side, he sat down. He sat around enough, cut up his knee, made ten arrows out of it. You left, and the morning of the second day I was sitting like this. At one time it looked like there was something like this at the door. Oh, oh. At one time it looked like my tent started to fall sideways. I just looked up, there was something my tent was leaning on sideways. Then he showed up in the tent. You look, and he is smiling and laughing. Having taken a step to the other side [of the tent], he sat down. He sat a little, having cut his knee, and made ten arrows out of it. The next morning he got up, and having dressed, he set out to chase the devil. Then the second time the old woman whiled away the day, when evening came, the youngest son came. Her son, having taken off his shoes and clothes, sat down. âSon, do you know something? The devil was here. The second morning I was sitting and it looked like there is something by the door, it looked like. One time my tent leaned to the side. I just looked up, some was pressing down on my tent. The old devil looked like it showed himself. From the street, having sat on that side of the tent, he cut his knee, and made ten arrows.
